content:
Hi everyone!
My background is in programming languages and compiler engineering, and I've been interested in abstract interpretation for a while. This project started as an attempt to build a relatively textbook-style
implementation of the core framework in Lean, using CSLib's LTS as the semantic foundation.

Repo: https://github.com/Maokami/absinterp

For the design I mostly followed Introduction to Static Analysis: An Abstract Interpretation Perspective (Rival & Yi) and Xavier Leroy's Mechanizing abstract interpretation
(https://xavierleroy.org/talks/N40AI.pdf).
AI disclosure: this was developed with substantial AI assistance (Claude Code / Codex). All proofs are machine-checked, and Claude-assisted commits carry Co-authored-by: Claude … trailers in the git history.

A quick tour of the pieces:

  • γ-only design. No α and no Galois connection required, soundness-first. The kernel ConcretizationDomain carries only gamma, gamma_monotone, gamma_top; meet/filter/backward/transfer come in as opt-in
    capabilities. A Galois connection isn't required, but there's an opt-in bridge that builds a ConcretizationDomain from a Mathlib GaloisConnection, so the γ-only kernel still connects to the classic picture
    when you want it.

  • Step → trace soundness. soundTrace_of_soundStep lifts local one-step soundness (plus monotonicity) to soundness of the whole lifted trace transformer, so a domain author only has to prove the local step.

  • CSLib LTS instantiation. LTSAbstraction bundles an LTS with a labeled transfer and a SoundStep proof and derives trace soundness from it; a parallel collecting interface wraps MTr / ωTr / HasTau with a
    post-fixpoint bridge. Kleene iteration and a widening operator are included too.

Domains and examples built on top:

  • Domains: Sign, Interval, Parity (under AbsInterp/Domains/).
  • An end-to-end IMP case study over the canonical IMP LTS (Examples/IMP/), covering both the labeled-trace path and an unlabeled collecting/fixpoint path, with Sign / Interval / widening showcases in
    Examples/IMP/Programs/.

I'd like to contribute this to CSLib incrementally, and wanted to ask whether you'd be open to taking a look. If there is any groundwork I should do first, or any design questions worth discussing up front, I'd be very glad to hear your thoughts.

Thanks!

@Jaeho Choi Regarding the use of AI tools, please read this carefully:
https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-role-of-ai

I took a quick look at your repo. I noticed that there is a lot of code about LTS in AbsInterp/Instances/LTS. Could you give a quick overview about what that code is about?

Also, what are the batches in which you expect to contribute your code to cslib?

Hi @Ching-Tsun Chou ,

(1) Thanks for pointing me to the AI policy!
I read it carefully, including the mathlib policy, and for any PRs, I will follow it: only submitting code that I have reviewed and fully understand, and disclosing AI-tool usage clearly.

(2) About AbsInterp/Instances/LTS: this is the LTS-specific instantiation of the generic abstract-interpretation framework. It connects my framework's notions of concrete post transformers, abstract transformers, and soundness to CSLib's existing LTS interface. It is not intended to reimplement LTS theory.

Semantics/ gives the framework a transformer view of a CSLib LTS. For example, postStep lts label is lts.setImage viewed as a one-step post transformer, and postAny lts is the label-erased collecting post.

Instantiation/ is the core part. LTSAbstraction packages a CSLib LTS, a concretization γ, a labeled abstract transfer, and a local one-step soundness proof: SoundStep (postStep lts) γ transfer.
The main theorem there is LTSAbstraction.soundTraceLifted. It is the CSLib-LTS specialization of the generic theorem soundTrace_of_soundStep: once an LTSAbstraction contains the local SoundStep proof, it derives SoundTrace for liftTracePost (postStep lts). The monotonicity side condition required by the generic theorem is handled by postStep_monotone for CSLib setImage.

Analyses/ contains helper code for analyses that observe states through a function such as read : State → Observation. The helper lets the user prove a direct transition-level condition and turn it into the framework-level SoundStep. The concrete Sign/Interval/Parity adapters are downstream examples, not what I would propose as the initial CSLib contribution.

(3) For contributions, I want to start small.

First, I would propose only the minimal CSLib-LTS soundness bridge: local one-step abstract soundness over a CSLib LTS implies finite labeled-trace soundness. Concretely, a per-label obligation postStep lts μ (γ a) ⊆ γ (transfer μ a) (SoundStep) yields SoundTrace for liftTracePost (postStep lts) over all finite label lists, via soundTrace_of_soundStep specialized to lts.setImage.

Second, if that shape is acceptable, I would propose the γ-based abstract-domain interface, currently called ConcretizationDomain: a concretization function, monotonicity, top coverage, and opt-in soundness capabilities for operations. The core would stay γ-only, with no required α or Galois connection; a Galois-connection bridge could be separate interop.

I would keep other features, such as IMP example, fixpoint, and widening as future material rather than part of the first PRs.

I'm inclined to think that the transformer view of LTS probably should be added to LTS itself, since it may have wider applicability. Let's wait and see what your PR looks like. Please add the references you are working from to references.bib and point to specific places in the references in code comments when appropriate. That will help the reviewers understand your code.
Thanks! I'll proceed with the PR in the direction you suggested, starting from the LTS side.
